newsitem.title: USA: Service Corp. drops bid for Loewen.
newsitem.headline: Service Corp. drops bid for Loewen.

text.p: Service Corp. International said Tuesday it was dropping its $2.9 billion bid for rival funeral home operator Loewen Group Inc.

Houston-based Service Corp., the largest funeral home operator in North America, cited Loewen's recent acquisition program, costs associated with Loewen's executive severance packages and uncertainties about divestitures that might be required to complete the transaction. Loewen, based in Vancouver, British Columbia, is Service Corp.'s biggest rival.

"The cumulative effect of actions taken by Loewen since our offer was announced, and the disclosure of details related to certain of Loewen's other transactions, have adversely impacted SCI's view of Loewen's value to SCI shareholders," Service Corp. Chairman R.L. Waltrip said in a statement.
"Consequently, rather than reducing our offer, SCI has decided not to pursue the acquisition of Loewen at this time."
Loewen has said it preferred to remain independent and had resisted the Service Corp. offer.

Loewen said in December that the Federal Trade Commission, the Canadian Competition Bureau and officials in several U.S. states had launched investigations into the potential antitrust implications of a deal.
